correctness.rationale: The proof uses the nonzero integral norm of the imaginary square-root linear form in its actual multiquadratic field, character orthogonality to obtain the exact conjugate second moment DQ, and AM-GM after isolating the identity and complex-conjugation factors. The formula specializes exactly to the recent full-sign bound when D=2^k, and the complete-basis specialization has D=2K. Supporting exact and finite computations agree with the theorem.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 primary source does not state a field-degree or negative-squareclass-rank refinement. Earlier separation-bound work already recognizes degree overestimation under algebraic dependence, so that general principle is not claimed as new. Searches did not find the explicit D-sensitive formula or the sharp K-1 complete-multiquadratic-basis exponent. Dubickas (2024) was not inspected in full and remains the principal residual literature risk because the 2026 primary source cites it for a related product argument.

value.rationale: The result changes the coefficient exponent from 2^{K-1}-1 to D/2-1 whenever the negative square classes are dependent. For the natural complete K-element basis of a multiquadratic field this gives the optimal fixed-radicand exponent K-1 with an explicit constant, converting an exponential-in-K exponent into a linear one.
